source: 768 Ferryman
target: 768 Ferryman

source: Lumian nodded, his right hand naturally falling on the Traveler’s Bag.
target: Lumian nutivit caput, et dextera manus eius naturaliter in sacco viatoris cecidit.

source: He then walked over to the dilapidated, gloomy boat, noticing the severely decayed boatman turning aside to make way, as if signaling for him to hurry aboard.
target: Tum accessit ad barcam decrepitae et lugubris, animadvertens nautam valde corruptum ad latus se vertere ut viam liberarent, quasi eum instanter conscendere hortaret.

source: “Can you ferry me across the Styx?” Lumian asked politely in Dutanese.
target: „Potesne me per Styx transferri?“ in Dutanensi sermone comiter rogavit Lumian.

source: Given that the former Death hailed from the Southern Continent, Lumian figured that speaking Dutanese might be more readily accepted by “all parties” in the Underworld.
target: Cum prior Mors ex Continente Meridionali proveniret, Lumian ratus est loqui Dutanensem, quod ab omnibus in Inferis partibus facilius recipi posset.

source: After all, in an environment so rich with the stench of death that a living person couldn’t last a second, using mystical languages like ancient Hermes, which could manipulate natural forces, might have unexpected effects.
target: Nam in ambitu odore mortis tam saturato ut nullus homo vivus ne momentum quidem maneret, usus linguarum mysticarum, ut veteris Hermetis, quae vires naturales regere poterant, effectus inopinatos ferre poterat.

source: For instance, merely uttering the words “River Styx” could forge a strong connection with the dark, ethereal river before him, possibly causing it to whip up a massive wave and sweep him away.
target: Exempli gratia, sola verba “Flumen Styx” pronuntiata firmum vinculum cum flumine obscuro et aethereo ante eum constituere posset, fortasse ita ut ingens unda excitata eum rapiret.

source: The boatman, its eye sockets filled with thick blood vessels and oozing yellow pus, faced the river, wide enough that the opposite bank was out of sight, and remained motionless.
target: Nauta, cuius orbitae oculorum crassis vasculis sanguine et fluxu flavo exorrebant, flumen respexit, latius satis ut altera ripa extra conspectum esset, et immotus mansit.

source: It seemed it was answering Lumian with his actions:
target: Videbatur se actis suis Lumiano respondere:

source: “Why would you try to communicate with a corpse?”
target: „Cur conaris cum cadavero colloqui?“

source: “I can’t hear you, nor can I make a sound.”
target: „Non te audīre possum, neque ullam vocem efficere.“

source: “It seems ordinary language won’t do… I’ve heard that the Death pathway includes a Language of the Dead, but unfortunately, I don’t speak it…” Lumian muttered to himself quietly as he let his eyes take on a silver-black hue and slowly stepped onto the rickety, gloomy boat.
target: „Videtur sermo vulgaris non sufficere… Audivi iter Mortis comprehendere Linguam Mortuorum, sed, pro dolor, eam non loquor…“ submurmuravit Lumian sibi ipsi quiete, dum oculos in nitore argenteo-nigro induit et lente in barcam labefactam lugubrem conscenderet.

source: In his Eye of Calamity, the boatman’s destiny was pure black, dead and void, showing no signs of change.
target: Sub aspectu Calamitatis, fatum nautae erat purum nigrum, mortuum et inane, nihil mutationis ostendens.

source: “Does this mean no matter how much the boatman struggles, it can’t change its status as a corpse, and its only fate is to wither away with time until even its existence vanishes?”
target: Num hoc significat quod, quamquam nauta quantumcumque laboret, statum cadaveris mutare non possit, nec aliud fatum eius sit nisi tempore evanescere, donec ipsa existentia dissolvatur?

source: “But that doesn’t mean the boatman can’t do anything during this time before its demise.”
target: Sed id non significat nautam in hoc tempore ante finem nihil agere posse.

source: “Its actions can still affect the fates of others, including mine and other undead beings.”
target: Eius actus tamen fata aliorum, inter mea et cetera corpora non viventium, afficere possunt.

source: “From this perspective, the boatman, or rather the summoned undead, should still have a destiny, only that the outcome cannot be changed…”
target: Ex hoc prospectu, nauta—vel potius evocatus non viventium—adhuc fatum habere debet, sed exitus immutabilis manet…

source: “Indeed, they have destinies, but my current rank isn’t high enough to see them, is it? After all, objects have destinies too, but I can’t see them now…”
target: Revera, fata habent; sed gradus meus nunc non satis altus est ad ea perspicienda, an non? Nam et res fata habent, sed nunc ea videre non possum…

source: “It might also be that the destinies of the dead need to interact with others to manifest in the destinies of those others…”
target: Forsitan etiam fata mortuorum cum aliis agere necesse habeant ut in fatibus illorum manifesta fiant…

source: “Perhaps because he had temporarily become an undead himself, Lumian couldn’t help but ponder the destinies of these “residents” of the Underworld.”
target: Forsitan quia ipse ad tempus in statum non viventium versa esset, Lumian cogitare de fatibus horum “incolarum” Inferorum non potuit non meditari.

source: “With the mystical knowledge he currently possessed, he couldn’t define destiny precisely, nor did he know how much the mercury river of fate encompassed, or whether there were unseen aspects or hidden parts he wasn’t aware of yet.”
target: Cum scientia mystica quam nunc haberet, fatum exacte definire non potuit, nec scivit quantum flumen mercuriale fatum complectat aut num partes invisibiles vel absconditas exsisterent de quibus nondum noscere valeat.

source: “He felt there must be, which stemmed from a few simple questions:”
target: Sentiebat tales esse necesse, a paucis quaestionibus simplicibus orta:

source: “Could it be that by donning the Eggers family’s golden mask and becoming an undead, the river of fate that still existed for me simply disappears, turning utterly black and void?”
target: Num fieri potest ut, induendo larvam auream familiae Eggers et factus in non viventem, flumen fatum, quod mihi adhuc subsistebat, omnino evanescat, se vertens in nigrellum et inane?

source: “And when I take off the mask, does the river of fate instantly return?”
target: Et cum larvam auferam, num flumen fatum statim revertitur?

source: “What then is the river of fate? A plaything at our disposal?”
target: Quid igitur est flumen fatum? An quasi ludibrium nobis tribuendum sit?

source: “Although the golden mask of the Eggers family was made by Death, it didn’t contain Beyonder characteristics and was only of a higher rank.”
target: Etsi larva aurea familiae Eggers a Morte confecta erat, proprietates Beyonder non continens, solum gradus superioris exhibebatur.

source: “It surely wasn’t simple enough to manipulate the river of fate so easily!”
target: Certe non erat satis simplex ut flumen fatum ita facile regere posset!

source: “Later on, if there’s a chance, I should have a Monster pathway Beyonder observe my fate to see the changes before and after donning the golden mask…”
target: Postea, si occasio obveniret, debebo Monstrum semitae Beyonder fatum meum observare ut mutationes ante larvam auream induendam et postea notentur…

source: “Uh… never mind, unless I find a demigod-level Monster pathway Beyonder, otherwise it would only harm them.
target: Heu… noli quaerere, nisi inveniam Beyonder ad gradum demidei in semita Monstrorum; alioquin tantum illis noceret.

source: “Even when I had only Mr. Fool’s seal, the false angelic rank, and the residual aura of the Blood Emperor, the patrol team’s ‘machine’ Kolobo from Port Pylos was already too afraid to look at me, thinking it would bring him great danger.”
target: Etiam cum solum sigillo Domini Stulti, falso ordine angelico, atque reliqua aura Imperatoris Sanguinis haberem, machina „Kolobo“ turmae speculatoriae ex Portu Pylos iam nimis timebat me inspicere, existimans magnum periculum illi afferre.

source: “Now, I have also added the Underworld Daoist’s seal and Omebella’s bloodline…”
target: Nunc quoque sigillum Taoistae Inferorum atque sanguinis Omebellae adieci…

source: “Lumian positioned himself at the center of the battered boat, allowing the golden mask to turn his eyes iron-black.”
target: Lumian se in media parte barcae laesa collocavit, permittens larvam auream oculos eius in ferreo nigros verti.

source: “He wanted to preemptively spot the boatman’s weaknesses to prepare for any potential mishaps.”
target: Volebat praevenire infirmitates nautae, ut ad quamlibet casus incertos se praepararet.

source: “At that moment, the highly decayed boatman began to row, slowly steering the dark boat towards the other side of the surreal, shadowy river.”
target: Illo momento, nauta, valde corruptus, remigare coepit, lente barcam obscuram versus alteram ripam fluminis surreali et umbrato gubernans.

source: “His body was entirely cloaked in dark colors, and Lumian struggled to find any sign of a vulnerable pale spot amid the black.”
target: Corpus eius totum in tenebrosis coloribus vestebatur, et Lumian differebat aliquem indicium vulnerabilis pallidae maculae intra nigredinem invenire.

source: “Of course, these dark colors also meant that the boatman was completely vulnerable to sunlight and lightning.”
target: Certe, hi colores obscuri etiam significabant nautam omnino subiectum radiis solis et fulminibus esse.

source: “The next second, Knight of Swords Maric’s voice rang in Lumian’s ears: ‘Its weaknesses might not be here.’”
target: Secundo postremo, vox equitis gladii Maric in auribus Lumiani sonuit: „Infirmitates eius hic fortasse non adsunt.“

source: “Not here? What do you mean they’re not here? Can weaknesses be separated from the person?”
target: Non hic? Quid hoc significas? Possunt infirmitates a persona separari?

source: “Just as Lumian was filled with intense curiosity, he remembered several stories his sister had once told him.”
target: Sicut Lumian vehementer curiositate repletus esset, meminit multarum fabularum quas soror eius olim narraverat.

source: “In those stories, a type of monster called a lich would create phylacteries and hide them in heavily protected, secret places.”
target: In illis fabulis, genus monstri, lich appellatus, phylactera creabat et ea in locis arcte custodiendis atque occultis recondebat.

source: “As long as the phylacteries were not found and destroyed, the lich would not truly die, effectively separating its fatal weakness from itself.”
target: Dum phylactera non deprehendantur nec deleri possint, lich vere non moriebatur, efficaciter fatalem infirmitatem a se separans.

source: (Amonoculus’ note: phylactery ⌜ either of two small square leather boxes containing slips inscribed with scriptural passages and traditionally worn on the left arm and on the head by observant Jewish men and especially adherents of Orthodox Judaism during morning weekday prayers.)
target: (Nota Amonoculi: “phylactery” – unum ex duobus parvis capsulis quadratis coriaceis, in quibus schedulae cum inscriptionibus sacris continentur, et quae more solito a viris Iudaeis observantibus—praesertim ab orthodoxis cultoribus—in brachio sinistro atque in capite geruntur, praesertim in precibus matutinis dierum hebdomadicorum.)

source: “And in the twenty-two paths of the divine, such things were hardly surprising.”
target: Et in viginti duobus itineribus divinis, talia vix mirabilia erant.

source: “The Knight of Swords continued, ‘Were you trying to discern its fate earlier?’”
target: Eques Gladii perrexit: „Num prius fatum eius quaerebas?“

source: “It holds a considerable rank; this is a dangerous endeavor.”
target: „Magnum gradum tenet; hoc res periculosa est.“

source: “A considerable rank? Lumian glanced at the boatman, draped in tattered clothes and highly decayed flesh, unable to see anything particularly formidable about it.”
target: „Magnus gradus?“ Lumian aspexit nautam, vestimentis lacerrimis et carne graviter corrupta indutum, nihil vere formidolosum in eo perspicuum esse censens.

source: “However, the fact that it could ferry across the River Styx without sinking into it certainly suggested something extraordinary.”
target: Attamen, quod Styx flumen transferre poterat sine se mergendo, certam aliquam rem extraordinariam significabat.

source: “Lumian diverted his gaze, closely watching the boatman’s every move, patiently waiting as the dilapidated boat made its way across the River Styx to the opposite shore.”
target: Lumian oculos avertit, omnes motus nautae diligenter inspiciens, patienter exspectans dum barca laesa per Styx flumen ad ripam alteram navigaret.

source: “The battered boat rocked slowly, as if it might fall apart at any moment, taking what felt like an eternity to reach the middle of the river.”
target: Barca laesa lente fremuit, quasi quovis momento dissolveri posset, atque quasi aeternitatem caperet ad medium fluminis perveniendum.

source: “Suddenly, the highly decayed boatman raised its long oar and turned toward Lumian.”
target: Subito, nauta valde corruptus longum remum elevavit et versus Lumian se vertit.

source: “As the gloomy boat came to a halt, the boatman’s mouth abruptly opened, splitting down to its decayed chest, its hollowed-out navel, and further down to its groin.”
target: Dum barca lugubris consederet, os nautae subito aperitum est, extendens se usque ad pectus corruptum, per umbilicum excavatum, et usque ad inguen.

source: “Its body unfolded like a coat unbuttoning, stretching out to the sides, revealing no darkened organs or bones of its own, but rather a heap of half-melted, decayed limbs.”
target: Corpus eius evolutum est quasi vestis soluta, latera pandens, non ostendens ulla obscurata viscera aut ossa sua, sed potius acervum membrorum dimidium liquefactorum et corruptorum.

source: “Once again, Lumian felt a chill that made him shudder, daring not to harbor any thoughts of resistance.”
target: Rursus, Lumian frigoris sensu pervultus est, qui eum trepidare fecit, ne auderet ullas cogitationes repugnationis fovere.

source: “He clenched his right hand, which had been ready.”
target: Dextram manum, quae praeparata iam erat, concluxit.

source: “He grasped the Sword of Courage from the Traveler’s Bag, holding the hilt of the iron-black broadsword.”
target: Gladium Fortitudinis ex sacco viatoris arripuit, manubrium gladii ferrei nigri tenens.

source: “Courage swiftly filled Lumian’s body, prompting a manic smile on his face.”
target: Fortitudo celeriter corpus Lumiani replevit, provocans risum insanum in facie eius.

source: “What is there to fear from a mere boatman?”
target: Quid est metuendum ab mero nauta?

source: “Even if Death Himself stood before me, I would strike Him down with my sword!”
target: Etiam si Mors ipse coram me steteret, eum gladio meo ferirem!

source: “Lumian drew his broadsword, now ablaze with white-blue flames, and slashed fiercely at the boatman, who was lunging at him with its skin peeled open.”
target: Lumian gladium suum extraxit, nunc flammis albo-caeruleis incensum, et ferociter nautam oppugnavit, qui ad eum impetum faciebat, cute expolita.

source: “With a thud, the Sword of Courage cut through the pile of melting limbs in the boatman’s stomach and struck the layer of rotting skin riddled with holes behind its chest.”
target: Cum strepitu, Gladius Fortitudinis per agger membrorum liquefactorum in stomacho nautae transectus est et ictum givit strata cutis putridae, foraminibus infixa, post pectus eius.

source: “But the broadsword failed to split the seemingly fragile, decayed skin.”
target: At gladium ferreum cutem, quae parum firma et corrupta videbatur, dividere non potuit.

source: “As Lumian readied a second strike, one accompanied by a massive explosion, the boatman swiftly recoiled, slowly closing its opened chest and abdomen.”
target: Dum Lumian secundum ictum parabat, cui magna explosio comitabat, nauta celeriter recedens, lente pectus et abdomina aperta claudebat.

source: “At the same time, the voice of the Knight of Swords rang in Lumian’s ears: ‘Stop. We’ve got it under control’”
target: Simul vox equitis gladii in auribus Lumiani sonuit: „Siste. Illud sub nostra potestate est.“

source: “This is our chance to finish it off!” Lumian responded without hesitation.
target: „Hoc est occasio nostra ut illud conficiamus!“ respondit Lumian sine cunctatione.

source: “He and the Knight of Swords were communicating in Intis.”
target: Ipse et Eques Gladii in lingua Intis colloquebantur.

source: “The Knight of Swords paused for a second and said, ‘I know, you’re not afraid of it, and you could kill it, but if it dies, we can’t cross the River Styx.’”
target: Eques Gladii paulisper cessavit et dixit: „Scio te id non timere nec non potuisse occidere; sed si moritur, Styx flumen transire non possumus.“

source: “Seeing Lumian calm down a bit, the Knight of Swords added, ‘Besides, killing it won’t grant you any Beyonder characteristics. It’s merely the skin of the true Ferryman. It seems to have been consuming other corpses, trying to regain a body but never succeeding.’”
target: Videns Lumian paululum se quietum reddi, Eques Gladii addidit: „Praeterea, eius interficere tibi nullas proprietates Beyonder conferet; solum cutis veri Ferryman est. Videtur alios cadavera vorasse, corpus restituere conans sed numquam succedere.“

source: “Lumian accepted the Knight of Swords’ explanation.”
target: Lumian explicationem Equitis Gladii accepit.

source: “Having courage didn’t mean being deaf to others’ words, it’s just selectively ignoring dangerous warnings.”
target: Fortitudo habita non significat aliorum verba non audire; sed potius monitiones periculosas selective ignorare.

source: “He then placed the Sword of Courage back among the ordinary straight swords in the Traveler’s Bag.”
target: Tum gladium Fortitudinis inter gladios ordinarios et rectos in sacco viatoris reponit.

source: “This time, he didn’t feel the post-event fear because this was the purpose of using the Sword of Courage. The only thing he feared was:”
target: Hoc tempore, metu post eventum non affectus est, nam hoc propositum usus Gladii Fortitudinis erat. Solum quod eum terruit fuit:

source: “A demigod’s skin has been peeled off? What in hell happened in the Underworld back then?”
target: Cutis demidei expolita est? Quid in Inferis tunc evenit?

source: “Lumian watched as the boatman slowly and struggle-fully pinched together the split skin and rotting flesh on its chest, like buttoning up a coat.”
target: Lumian observabat nauta, lente et strenue, cute scissa et carne putrescente in pectore congregare, quasi vestem fibulari conaretur.

source: “Following this, the boatman plunged its long, dark, decayed oar into the surreal shadowy River Styx, moving it at an even slower pace as if resisting something.”
target: Post hoc, nauta longum, obscurum et corruptum remum in flumen Styx surreale et umbratum immergit, eo multo tardius movere videtur quasi aliquid oppresseret.

source: “Has the demigod of the temperance faction possessed the boatman, forcefully taking control and making it continue to row? It looks like this control is met with strong resistance… Lumian remained ready to draw the Sword of Courage again in case of any unforeseen incidents.”
target: Num demideus factionis temperantiae nautam possiderit, vehementer imperium sumens atque remigare perpetuare coercens? Videor hoc imperium cum valida oppositione occurri… Lumian paratus remansit gladium Fortitudinis iterum extrahere, si quid inopinatum accideret.

source: “As the gloomy boat rocked its way towards the opposite shore of the Styx, Lumian, having nothing better to do, started a conversation with the Knight of Swords.”
target: Dum barca lugubris viam suam ad ripam oppositam Styx navigabat, Lumian, nihil melius agens, colloquium cum Equite Gladii inire coepit.

source: “I saw the entire Underworld as a series of descending layers earlier. Crossing the Styx should just get us to the other side of this layer, so why did you say it’s like entering deep into the Underworld?”
target: „Totum Infernum vidi ut seriem stratorum decrescentium antea. Transire Styx nos solummodo ad ripam huius strata deducere debet; cur ergo dixisti hoc simile esse ingressui in profunda Inferna?“

source: “The Knight of Swords simply replied, ‘The geography of the Underworld doesn’t completely align with the real world. According to the many notes of the Eggers family, there are two ways to enter the depths of the Underworld. The first is to descend layer by layer through the worlds encircling the Styx, which are used to punish sinners, ultimately arriving at the realm where the Blessed of Death reside. The second is to cross the Styx directly.’”
target: Eques Gladii simpliciter respondit: „Geographia Inferni non perfecte congruit cum mundo reali. Secundum multas notas familiae Eggers, duo modi sunt ad intrandum profunditates Inferni. Primo stratum post stratum per mundos circa Styx qui ad peccatores puniendos adhibentur descendi debet, tandem ad regnum ubi beati Mortis resident; secundo vero Styx directe transiri oportet.“

source: “Is that so…” Lumian mused aloud, “So, our destination is the realm once inhabited by the Blessed of Death?”
target: „Sic ergo…” meditatus audibiliter est Lumian, „Ergo, propositum nostrum est regnum, quod olim a Beatis Mortis incolatum erat?“

source: “The Knight of Swords paused for a second and said, ‘Death’s palace should be there as well.’”
target: Eques Gladii paulisper cessavit et dixit: „Palatium Mortis ibi quoque esse debet.“

source: “The palace of the former Death? Lumian’s eyelids twitched at the thought.”
target: „Palatium prioris Mortis?“ Palpebra Lumiani ad hanc rem subitam contrahere coeperunt.

source: “As he and the Knight of Swords alternated between silence and conversation, the boundary on the other side of the Styx finally came into view.”
target: Dum ille et Eques Gladii inter silentia atque sermonem alternabantur, limen contra Styx tandem in conspectum venit.
